Theorem

Theorem 1.35\group harmonic-functions Source: han-lin-lecture-notes:page-0023, han-lin-lecture-notes:page-0024 ↗ hanlin:thm-subharmonic-max ↗ hanlin:corollary-harnack-ball If $u\in C(\overline{B_1})$ is harmonic in $B_1$ and has a strict maximum at $x_0\in \partial B_1$, then \[ \partial _nu(x_0)\ge c(n)\bigl(u(x_0)-u(0)\bigr). \]
Proof

\sketch On the annulus $B_1\setminus \overline{B_{1/2}}$ use the subharmonic barrier $v=e^{-\alpha |x|^2}-e^{-\alpha }$ and apply the maximum principle to $u-u(x_0)+\varepsilon v$. Corollary 3 supplies a uniform gap on $B_{1/2}$; choosing $\varepsilon $ proportional to that gap and differentiating the boundary comparison gives the normal derivative bound.

□
